newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish, Dutch banks silent on merger rumours.
newsitem.headline: Swedish, Dutch banks silent on merger rumours.

text.p: Swedish and Dutch banks on Thursday declined to comment on merger and acquisition rumours which drove bank share prices up on the Stockholm bourse.
"We don't have a comment, we never comment on share movements," said a spokesman for Nordbanken, variously rumoured to be merging with S-E-Banken or a takeover target for Dutch bank ABN Amro.
"We don't comment on market rumours," an ABN Amro spokesman said.
The main beneficiary of the talk was Handelsbanken, which was not rumoured to be merging with anybody.
It touched a high of 236 crowns, up 10.50 from Wednesday's 225.50, before settling back in the late afternoon to 231.50, still a 2.6 percent rise.
Dealers attributed the rise to the belief that Handelsbanken was likely to win market share in the event of a merger between its rivals.
Nordbanken rose 4.5 crowns to 269.50, S-E-Banken rose 0.5 crown to 81.00 and ABN Amro slipped 2.40 guilders on the Amsterdam market, to 134.40.
